And when they go to war, they think the gods are also at war. If you lose, your god is inferior to theirs. This creates a hierarchy of gods. To maintain peace, you must obey their god if you lose. This is called a pantheon. In the Greek pantheon, Zeus is at the top with Apollo, Aries, and Aphrodite as lower gods. Before, they were separate gods who fought in wars; the winners became the children of Zeus.

Men go to war because young men without families are discarded due to resource shortages. These young men raid other societies for wives to survive. Young women are not discarded as they have value in their society, whereas young men become like wolves, pillaging villages. This leads to the origin of war.

This pantheon leads to polytheism, then monotheism with the rise of the Roman Empire and Christianity. Monotheism allows empires to enforce their religion on others because humans are no longer seen as the most precious resource. The view of mind leading to matter in ancient civilizations differs from our belief that matter creates the mind.
